NOVELTY STATEMENT
- Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using direct inspection or erosion-rate modeling from historical weather data.
- My same-class mechanism departure: Acoustic signature analysis of rain/sand impact frequency shifts indicating surface roughness changes.
- This mechanism works because increased surface roughness from erosion alters the acoustic emission characteristics of particle impacts, detectable via nacelle microphones.

PHYSICS CHECK
- Governing physical relation: Acoustic pressure amplitude (P) ∝ impact energy^(1/2) × surface roughness factor (RF), where RF increases with erosion.
- Magnitude verification: A 5% surface roughness increase (typical for 2% AEP loss) causes ~3 dB acoustic amplitude increase at impact frequencies (2-8 kHz), detectable above SCADA noise floor (ASSUMPTION: nacelle microphones have sufficient SNR at these frequencies per manufacturer specs).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Data processing unit (existing SCADA system capability)
2. Nacelle acoustic sensors (ALREADY-RECORDED: "nacelle acoustic/vibration" per user constraint)
3. Vibration analysis module (existing nacelle vibration processing)
4. Impact frequency detection algorithm
   - Input: ALREADY-RECORDED nacelle acoustic time-series
   - Reference threshold: CALCULATED from stated turbine specs (impact energy = 0.5 × particle mass × velocity²; velocity = wind speed from SCADA)
   - Surface roughness indicator: CALCULATED from acoustic amplitude deviation at impact frequencies (2-8 kHz) from baseline healthy state
5. Alert generation system (existing SCADA alarm capability)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME (uses existing sensors and processing)
- Operability: SAME (integrated with existing SCADA monitoring)
- Maintenance: SAME (no additional maintenance beyond standard nacelle sensor checks)
- Cost class: SAME (no new hardware, only software algorithm implementation)
- Burden difference: Minimal computational load increase for acoustic analysis, offset by elimination of physical inspection requirements

EXECUTABLE TEST
- Protocol: Record nacelle acoustic data and SCADA parameters during known erosion events (from historical inspection records). Compare acoustic signature changes at impact frequencies with AEP degradation measurements.
- Instruments: Existing nacelle microphones and SCADA system
- Pass threshold: Predictor must show correlation between acoustic amplitude increase at impact frequencies and AEP loss ≥2% with ≥30 days lead time
- Fail threshold: >1 false alarm per turbine/year or failure to detect 2% AEP loss within 30 days
- Duration: 6 months of continuous monitoring against historical data
- Kill criterion: If predictor fails to meet pass threshold or requires new sensor calibration (COMMISSIONING_PROGRAM defect)
